# scoop-boot package list TEMPLATE for DevOps and infrastructure (delivered by
# scoop-boot.ps1 --update; do not edit). Not used directly: scoop-boot.ps1
# --package-template=devops copies it to etc\packages\<hostname>.txt, which then
# replaces default.txt on this machine (edit the copy, it is never updated).
# Same format as default.txt: one manifest per line in install order, "#" starts a
# comment. Bootstrap packages (7zip, git, aria2, sudo, ...) are installed before.
# Compared with default.txt: cloud, infrastructure-as-code, network and server
# tools instead of compilers, build tools and IDEs.

# System libraries
vcredist2022

# Browser (Azure portal, Entra admin center)
firefox

# Shells and scripting
pwsh
python314

# Azure (Service Bus Explorer: dead letters, resubmit; Storage Explorer: blobs, file shares)
azure-cli
azcopy
servicebusexplorer
azurestorageexplorer

# Infrastructure as code
terraform
tflint
terraform-docs
trivy

# Kubernetes is left out: Container Apps are managed with azure-cli. For AKS add
# kubectl, kubelogin and helm to the host copy.

# GitHub
gh

# Data formats and HTTP (Postman: API and health-endpoint checks)
jq
yq
curl
postman

# Network diagnostics: port scan and ncat (nmap), packet capture (wireshark),
# TCP port check through firewalls (tcping), traceroute with loss per hop
# (trippy), DNS queries against a chosen server (doggo, dig from bind), TLS and
# certificate check (sslscan), bandwidth (iperf3). Sysinternals adds psping,
# tcpview and whois.
nmap
wireshark
tcping
trippy
doggo
bind
sslscan
iperf3

# Remote access
openssh
putty
winscp
mremoteng

# Databases (clients)
go-sqlcmd
postgresql
dbeaver

# Security
openssl
keepass

# Editors and terminal
vscode
windows-terminal
notepadplusplus
winmerge

# Command line tools
ripgrep
fd

lazygit

# Windows tools
sysinternals
everything
greenshot
